prize_parts.citation: for proposing and realising quantum computation and simulation with trapped ions

statement.case_for: The Cirac-Zoller proposal turned laser-cooled trapped ions into a concrete platform for quantum gates and simulation, and the Innsbruck programme under Blatt and others delivered the first full gate demonstrations, multi-ion entanglement and later digital and analogue simulation. This is a complete arc from an original idea to thirty years of independent confirmation by several groups and to commercial machines. It is distinct in scope from the 2012 prize for controlling single quantum systems, because the question here is computation and simulation. It also has broad support across the committee (second place for Kroll, Lindroth and me), and it avoids the field-concentration problem that follows a second superconducting-circuit award so soon after 2025.
statement.case_against: The Cirac-Zoller gate itself is no longer the leading experimental gate, and the three-name credit leaves out Wineland-lineage and Monroe-type contributions, so the experimental share is not uniquely Blatt's. The prize may also look like an extension of 2012. Cirac and Zoller are credited on B020 as well, which would complicate any later optical-lattice award. By comparison B021 has the strongest opening support and a cleaner theory-plus-experiment split.

responses.point: Eriksson ranks magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene first because the Bistritzer-MacDonald prediction and the 2018 experiments give a clean theory-plus-experiment pair and opened a new platform.
responses.response: I agree the attribution is cleaner than for most candidates and that B021 is my fourth choice, so I keep it as an alternative. My reservation is maturity: the pairing mechanism is unsettled and the experimental credit is shared with Cao and other groups outside the credited names. Trapped ions have thirty years of replication behind them. I would not oppose B021 if the committee wants a materials prize, but I do not think it is more secure than B006.

responses.point: Danielsson ranks the topological-insulator case first as the clearest example of predicted and then confirmed new quantum matter, with Kane, Mele and Molenkamp as the originating theory plus first experiment.
responses.response: I share the view that B030 is conceptually excellent; I ranked it third. My concern is attribution: the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal that Molenkamp's experiment tested is not among the credited names, and Hasan's 3D work is a rival claim. A prize that omits BHZ risks a visible injustice, whereas the trapped-ion attribution gap is smaller. I would revisit B030 if colleagues can show the BHZ role is adequately covered by the three-name credit.

responses.point: Lindroth ranks optical lattice clocks first and trapped-ion computation second, valuing the atomic-physics depth and noting the relation to the 2012 prize.
responses.response: We agree on B006 and on the need to defend it against the 2012 overlap. I would argue that Wineland and Haroche were honoured for measurement and control of individual quantum systems, whereas the new citation is about gate-based computation and simulation. I am more cautious about B024: the clock result is excellent but the 10^-18 milestone involves several groups beyond Katori and Ye, and the sequence of AMO prizes in 2005 and 2012 already covers much of precision spectroscopy.

responses.point: Pearce ranks topological insulators first and notes that the three-person limit omits legitimate contributors, while placing optical-lattice simulation third.
responses.response: I accept the allocation caution and apply it to my own choice: for B006 the three names cover the decisive proposal and the early experiment but leave Monroe and Wineland-lineage work to the citation wording. I would keep the citation on the proposal and realisation to make that limit explicit. On B020, I see it as closely related to B006 through Cirac and Zoller, so awarding both would be a poor use of the same names.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts trapped-ion computation as distinct from the 2012 prize.
Whether Blatt is the right experimental laureate or other trapped-ion experimentalists should be credited instead.
How to handle Cirac and Zoller appearing on both B006 and B020.
Whether a second superconducting-circuit prize (B002) should be considered at all so soon after 2025, which I cannot judge impartially.
statement.conflict_note: Possible recusal issue: B002 (circuit QED) is close to my own field at Chalmers and WACQT, and I work with Per Delsing and Anton Frisk Kockum on related circuit and waveguide QED; Chalmers hosted researchers associated with the 2025 prize. I therefore discount my own opening first choice and recommend that I take no decisive role on B002. No specific conflict is apparent for B006, B021 or B030 from the provided profile.
